promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 10 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Your knee pain changes the plan: please see a sports physio this week, swap the tempo for cross-training, and keep running easy and flat while we see how it settles.

answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
I can't tell you whether it is your IT band, and I shouldn't guess, because outer-knee pain that is sharp on downhills and sore on stairs has a few possible causes. Please book a sports physio this week so you get a proper look before we add more load. In the meantime, treat it as something to respect, not run through.

No tempo on Wednesday. With a new, sharp pain that stopped a run, a threshold session is the wrong thing to stack on top. I've swapped it for cross-training so you keep the aerobic work without pounding the knee, and we can bring quality back once the physio clears you and you've had a few pain-free easy runs.

new.analysis:
You followed the plan all week until the long run, where the knee forced an early stop at 8.5 mi and a walk home, so the big miss was 4 mi of long-run time on feet rather than anything you did wrong. Tuesday's easy, Wednesday's threshold and Thursday's easy all landed as planned, and Saturday's 4 mi went in clean. The knee note on Thursday's hill is the first sign in the data, so this has been building for a few days rather than appearing out of nowhere.

The right call now is to back off running load for a week while you get the knee looked at, not to try to make up the missed miles. Your fitness is in good shape: easy pace is trending down at the same heart rate, and the Aug 9 long run held 10:00/mi with only a small drift, which is encouraging for sub-3:45. One quiet week will not cost you that; one week of pushing through outer-knee pain can.

That is why next week has no tempo, a cross-training day in its place, and a flat long run capped at 10 mi with permission to shorten it if the pain returns. If the physio clears you and the easy runs feel clean, we will put a marathon-pace segment back into the long run the following week and build from there. If the knee is still barking, tell me on Sunday and we will adjust again rather than force the next step.

safetyCallouts.title: See a sports physio about the right knee.
safetyCallouts.body: New sharp pain on the outside of the knee that worsens on downhills and aches on stairs deserves a professional look before more hard running. Stop any run if the sharp pain comes back, and don't push through it. Tell them about the Sunday long run and the stair ache, and ask what you can safely do this week.
